title: T25 desktop: Remember this — offer, checkboxes and Yes in chat and the quick box
head: t25-remember-desktop
body:
**needs Braden** — ask-first gate (T25)

## What
Desktop half of T25 "Remember this", built against the agent-core 0.7.21 contract (docs/t25/core.md §5).
- When a reply's `done` carries `remember_offer`, the full app chat (`Chat.tsx`) and the quick box (`QuickApp.tsx`) show one "Want me to remember that?" card (new `src/components/RememberCard.tsx`, on the existing plan-card look and Lantern tokens). Each fact shows the service's own plain line. Several facts get one checkbox each, and all start checked (contract §5).
- It is the same two-call ask-first shape as onboarding and delete (#68). `POST /remember {offer_id, checked}` runs when the card shows and again on every checkbox change. Yes stays off until the preview for exactly the checked facts has come back, matching line for line. Yes then sends `{offer_id, checked, preview_id, confirm_token}` for that preview, once; a double click still sends once.
- No calls `POST /remember/decline`. If she ignores the card, her next message closes it. Either way nothing is saved.
- If the token is used or stale, the save could not finish, or OASIS is paused, the card ends in one calm plain sentence and saves nothing.
- Never more than one prompt (#29). A second offer while one is open is dropped, not stacked or swapped (§4 Q3). An offer is not shown next to a live plan card.
- Offers come only from `done.remember_offer`, checked by the new `parseRememberOffer`. Reply text, tool-result text and any other frame type never make an offer.
- The client gains `rememberPreview` / `rememberConfirm` / `rememberDecline`. The fake service gains both routes with single-use tokens bound to one offer, one preview and the exact checked ids.
- No new dependency. Main CSS is 77.29 / 11.75 kB (budget 78 / 12, #178). Quick CSS is 35.71 / 6.45 kB.

## Checks
<!-- swarm:checks -->

## Mutation check
| Mutant | Killing test (tests/remember.test.tsx, both surfaces unless noted) |
|---|---|
| Send the confirm as soon as the offer shows | T1 (a plain-words preview; showing it saves nothing), T2, T4 |
| Send unchecked facts on Yes | T2 (three checkboxes; only the checked ones are sent and saved), T5 (newest token after a toggle) |
| Send twice on a double click | T5 (exactly the previewed fact, once, even on a double click) |
| Drop the token (send `''`) | T2, T5, T6 |
| Send a different token | T2, T5, T6 |
| Keep the first token after a toggle | T2, T5 (newest token after a toggle) |
| Let a second prompt stack or swap (app chat) | T3 (a second offer never stacks), full app chat |
| Let a second prompt stack or swap (quick box) | T3 (a second offer never stacks), quick box |
| Show the offer next to a live plan card (app chat / quick box) | T3 (never next to a live plan card), each surface |
| Build an offer from reply or tool-result text (app chat / quick box) | T7 (only from the service event), each surface |
| No also sends a Yes | T4 (No sends nothing to save) |

13 of 13 killed, 0 survivors. Each mutant was applied alone by editing, then `npx vitest run tests/remember.test.tsx` was run, then the edit was restored.

## Tests
New `tests/remember.test.tsx` has 12 cases, each run on both the full app chat and the quick box, plus `parseRememberOffer` shape checks:
- T1: one offer with a plain preview and no internal words; only call 1 is sent.
- T2: three checkboxes, all checked; only the checked ones are sent and saved; with none checked, Yes is off.
- T3: no stacking; never next to a live plan card.
- T4: No, and ignoring the card, save nothing.
- T5: Yes sends exactly the previewed fact with its own token, once; after a toggle it sends the newest token.
- T6: a stale or used token gives a calm message and saves nothing; a failed save gives a plain message.
- T7: an offer comes only from `done.remember_offer`, never from text or another frame.

The full suite (`npm test`) still passes.

## Mac check
Tell Beacon "my birthday is March 3" and the offer shows. Yes saves it, and a later chat knows it. No saves nothing.
